oewn-01023429-v.learner: to reach a decision after talking about something or thinking it over carefully.
examples: After two days of talking it over, the jury concluded that he was not guilty.

oewn-01073784-v.learner: to come to an agreement about something.
examples: The two countries concluded a trade agreement last year.

oewn-02707070-v.learner: to be able to hold a certain amount or number inside.
examples: The hall can contain up to three hundred people.

oewn-01133899-v.learner: to hold back something such as a danger or an enemy, and stop it from spreading or gaining more power.
examples: Firefighters worked all night to contain the fire.

oewn-02753162-v.learner: to be a number that another number divides into exactly.
examples: Twelve contains both three and four.

oewn-06206950-n.learner: the general way in which something tends to develop.
examples: Her early love of science set the direction of her whole career.

oewn-06663446-n.learner: something that gives you advice about what to decide or what to do.
examples: The new teacher looked to her older colleagues for direction.
The direction of the family business was left to her son.

oewn-00816981-n.learner: the act of choosing a course and keeping to it.
examples: With firm direction from the captain, the boat kept a straight course through the storm.

oewn-07184131-n.learner: a formal statement ordering someone to do something.
examples: The judge gave the jury a direction to ignore the remark.

oewn-05712641-n.learner: the act of putting your attention or energy on something.
examples: After he left school, he felt he had no direction in his life.

oewn-13796315-n.learner: a small amount of something that is still enough to notice.
examples: Add a hint of lemon juice to the sauce.

oewn-06664322-n.learner: a sign or piece of information that points to a possible chance or opportunity.
examples: A friend gave him a hint about a job opening at the bank.
An old man walking his dog was a familiar sight in the village.

oewn-82981785-n.learner: a place that is interesting, especially to people visiting it.
examples: We spent the day seeing the sights of Rome.

oewn-00883327-n.learner: the act of looking, seeing, or watching.
examples: At first sight, the house seemed empty.

oewn-06220699-n.learner: how far someone can see with the mind; the way things look to them.
examples: All people are equal in the sight of the law.

oewn-13796604-n.learner: a large number, a large amount, or a large extent, often followed by 'of'.
examples: The new house cost a sight more than they had planned.

oewn-00701251-v.learner: to make someone reach a decision.
examples: The heavy rain decided us to stay at home.

oewn-05655001-n.learner: the quality of being rash and foolish, acting without careful thought or good sense.
examples: Trying to cross the mountains in winter was pure folly.

connotation.why: names conduct as foolish, a verdict built into the word

oewn-01756303-v.learner: to bring something out or give it, the way a tree gives fruit.
examples: The old apple tree still produces fruit every year.

oewn-02161530-v.learner: to bring something out for sale, or release it to the public.
examples: The studio produced three films last year.

oewn-01743695-v.learner: to grow something, often using farming methods to make it better.
examples: This region produces most of the country's rice.

oewn-00094214-v.learner: to come to have a physical feature, or to go through a change in one.
examples: Male deer produce a new set of antlers every year.

oewn-00654017-v.learner: to identify something, for example a plant or animal in science, and say what kind it is.
examples: The beetle was first described by scientists in 1850.
Dining with friends is her favourite way to spend an evening.
